framing_rule: M0 (frozen LCDM background, Omega_m=0.31115, screening/symmetron sector deleted) is a HYPOTHESIS CHANGE, not a derivation from K3xT2. Agreement below means 'consistent with M0's linear P(k) + linear bias + lognormal field at the level of this test' -- NOT a K3xT2 confirmation, and it does not touch mu_sym, c4_pta_product or any LeanMaster octad/moonshine construction (none exists as a galaxy-clustering observable; see E4's report and REPORT.md).

mask.note: mask built from the OBSERVED galaxy (ra,dec), not the ra/dec bounding rectangle -- avoids this project's earlier round-1 bounding-box artifact.

poisson_null_i.method: angles drawn uniformly (in solid angle) from the HEALPix-occupied footprint via rejection sampling; r drawn uniform-in-comoving-volume within the SAME shell window [r_lo,r_hi] used to select the data (E5's SELECTION_SHELL_IDX). Independent of the data's actual (ra,dec) pairs and independent of its actual n(z) beyond the flat-in-volume shell window -- unlike E5's z-shuffle null, this ALSO randomises angle.

xi_r_and_bias.fit_method: b^2 = sum(xi_data*xi_lin)/sum(xi_lin^2) over the fit range ONLY, ordinary least squares; NEVER fit to any topological statistic (per ground rules).
xi_r_and_bias.sanity_note: SDSS main-sample galaxies at z~0.05-0.1 are expected b~1.1-1.3 in the literature (L, quoted as a sanity band, not a fetched table); b_fit=0.856 is OUTSIDE -- treat mock comparison with caution that band.

lognormal_field.recipe: P_target=b^2*P_lin*exp(-(k*R_smooth)^2/2)*[k<=k_nyq], R_smooth=1 grid cell -> xi_target=pk2xi(P_target) -> xi_G=ln(1+xi_target) -> P_G=xi2pk(xi_G) -> delta_G~GRF(P_G) -> delta_LN=exp(delta_G-sigma_G^2/2)-1
lognormal_field.transform_method: 1D trapezoidal quadrature of the k^2 P(k) sinc(kr) Hankel integral (validated in this run's scratch calibration against a toy power-law P(k): round-trip recovery within a few percent; GRF normalisation validated the same way, measured P(k) of a realized field matched the input P(k) to <6% on a single 64^3 realization).

lognormal_grid.measured_wedge_fraction_method: Monte Carlo, 300000 uniform probe points over the box run through the SAME mask_and_shell_keep() filter the mocks use (replaces an earlier analytic solid-angle formula that was wrong by a factor of ~3 -- see calibrate_n_bar's docstring).
lognormal_grid.note: grid covers only the survey wedge's padded bounding box (not a symmetric NxNxN cube spanning the whole survey depth), which keeps n_cells small and avoids wasting >75% of a cube's volume outside the wedge.

lognormal_gate.definition: RMS over r in (20.0, 60.0) Mpc/h of z_i=(xi_mock_mean_i-xi_data_i)/sigma_total_i, where sigma_total combines the DATA's own Poisson shot-noise error ((1+xi)/sqrt(DD), Landy & Szalay 1993) with the 22-mock standard error of the mean, in quadrature. PASS iff RMS(z) < 3.0. This gate MUST pass for the Betti-curve comparison below to be treated as diagnostic of anything (ground rules / advisor review requirement). A raw amplitude ratio is also reported for the record but is NOT the pass/fail criterion (see GATE_Z_THRESHOLD constant's comment for why: it diverges at this fit range's zero-crossings).

lognormal_mocks_iii.interpretation: THIS (not the z-shuffle or Poisson-null envelopes above) is the actual M0 test per the ground rules. p close to the resolution floor (rank=0, i.e. the real L2 exceeds every leave-one-out mock L2) is the strongest evidence THIS TEST can give against 'consistent with M0's linear P(k)+bias+lognormal field'; a mid-range p is a match at this N, this scale range, and this (approximate) mock recipe -- consistent with M0 at the level of this test, NOT a K3xT2 confirmation. A mismatch concentrated below ~4-6 Mpc/h (this sample's mean inter-galaxy spacing, ~5.0 Mpc/h) is expected: lognormal mocks reproduce the 1-point PDF and 2-point function but not higher-order correlations or true void/filament shapes, and that scale is shot-noise dominated at N=25000 in this volume regardless.

final_synthesis_added_after_run: The xi(r) gate (see lognormal_gate) FAILED: RMS(z)=%.2f > threshold %.1f, computed AFTER the full run over all 22 mocks (this field is added post-hoc, referencing only numbers already computed above; no data or threshold was changed after seeing this). Per this script's own PRE-STATED design ('this gate MUST pass for the Betti-curve comparison below to be treated as diagnostic of anything'), the lognormal_mocks_iii rank p-values (p=0.043, the resolution floor, for H0, H1 AND H2 -- the real Betti curves differ from the mock ensemble by more than mock-to-mock scatter, at the maximum resolution 22 mocks give) must NOT be read as a clean M0 test. The gate failure means the CAMB-linear-P(k)+single-bias+lognormal recipe does not itself reproduce the data's own two-point function xi(r) to within combined shot-noise+mock-scatter uncertainty over r in [20,60] Mpc/h (b_fit=0.856 is also below the literature sanity band for SDSS main-sample galaxies, 1.1-1.3, another symptom of the same mismatch). The most defensible reading: at N=25000 in this survey volume, a SIMPLE lognormal mock (single linear bias, no higher-order corrections) is not an adequate null model for this catalogue's clustering amplitude/shape, so the downstream topology mismatch cannot be cleanly attributed to a cosmological effect (still less to K3xT2 -- no such observable is constructed here, per the framing rule) rather than to the mock recipe's own known limitations (single linear bias, no nonlinear/higher-order corrections, no fibre-collision modelling, modest survey volume raising cosmic variance in the very xi(r) the bias and gate are computed from). This is the honest conclusion this specific test supports: NEITHER a confirmation nor a rejection of M0 -- a diagnosed limitation of THIS mock recipe at THIS N, reported rather than concealed, per the ground rules' evidence-bound and pre-registered-statistic requirements. The Poisson-null and z-shuffle comparisons above remain valid as pipeline sanity checks (data is topologically further from unclustered noise than from a mock with at least some clustering, as expected) but are not the M0 test either.

post_hoc_advisor_review_checks.note: The three checks below were run AFTER the full 22-mock analysis, at an independent reviewer's request, to distinguish a pipeline bug from a genuine data feature. Each reads only already-fixed code/data; none changed any threshold, statistic or mock after seeing the headline result (GATE_Z_THRESHOLD=3.0 and STAT_R_RANGE were fixed before this run, per the script's own docstring, and are unchanged here).

sigma8_absolute_normalisation_check.method: sigma8(z=0) recomputed from this script's own kh/pk(CAMB) arrays via a top-hat window (R=8 Mpc/h) and the SAME trapezoidal quadrature style as pk2xi/xi2pk, compared to CAMB's own reported sigma8(z=0)=0.8118 (pre-rescale). This checks ABSOLUTE normalisation, which the pk2xi<->xi2pk ROUND-TRIP test already in this report cannot (a constant multiplicative error cancels in a round trip).
sigma8_absolute_normalisation_check.conclusion: No normalisation bug in the shared P(k)<->xi(r) transform. xi_lin, b_fit and sigma_G^2 are built on a correctly normalised P(k); the low b_fit is a real feature of this fit, not a units/normalisation artifact.

bias_sanity_band_correction.issue: This report's xi_r_and_bias.sanity_note originally quoted b~1.1-1.3 as the SDSS expectation, which is the SAMPLE-WIDE main-sample value, not appropriate for this shell (z~0.055-0.08, flux-limited to sub-L*/M_r~-19.5, faint-dominated galaxies, for which b~0.9-1.0 is the more relevant literature range). b_fit=0.856 is close to (very slightly below) that corrected band, not far outside it.
bias_sanity_band_correction.redshift_space_caveat: Separately: xi_data is measured in REDSHIFT SPACE (from observed z), while xi_lin is a REAL-SPACE model. The Kaiser boost (1+2beta/3+beta^2/5) at beta=f/b~0.59 is ~1.47, so the REAL-SPACE-equivalent bias implied by this fit is b_fit/sqrt(1.47)~0.71 -- genuinely low. This mismatch (fitting a real-space model to a redshift-space measurement) is an un-corrected simplification of this pipeline, and the more likely source of the low fitted bias than any normalisation error (see the sigma8 check above).
bias_sanity_band_correction.source_fix: e5b_lognormal_and_poisson_null.py's sanity_note text and the pass/fail band were corrected in the source for future runs; NOT re-run here since it is documentation of an existing number, not a change to any computed quantity.

angular_vs_3d_origin_of_the_xi_bump_at_r.issue: xi_data(r) is non-monotonic: declines from 0.070 (r=21) to ~0.012 (r=33), rises back to ~0.019 (r=41), then declines again. Smooth LCDM does not produce this shape (BAO is at ~105 Mpc/h, not 40); at this shell's distance (~200 Mpc/h), 10 degrees on the sky is ~35 Mpc/h transverse, so an uncorrected ANGULAR selection/completeness pattern on ~10-degree scales could produce exactly this bump, and this run's HEALPix mask is a binary occupied/not-occupied footprint with no completeness weighting (none is available: the catalogue has only ra, dec, z, zErr).
angular_vs_3d_origin_of_the_xi_bump_at_r.test: Recomputed the DATA's own LS xi(r), same real galaxies, same r_edges, but with the RANDOM catalogue replaced by data/real2/cosmic_web/sdss_dr17_random_shuffled_z_*.csv restricted to the same shell window (57854 points, ~2.3x oversample, vs this report's main 4x mask-uniform random) -- that catalogue carries the data's EXACT (ra,dec) pairs, so any purely angular selection/completeness effect divides out of the LS estimator by construction, isolating whether the bump is angular or 3D.

result.xi_with_mask_uniform_random_for_comparis: see xi_r_and_bias.xi_data in this same report

angular_vs_3d_origin_of_the_xi_bump_at_r.conclusion: The bump PERSISTS (dip near r=33, secondary rise to ~0.01-0.012 at r=39-45) with the angular-position-MATCHED random, at somewhat lower overall amplitude than with the mask-uniform random. Per the diagnostic logic: persistence under an angular-matched random means this is NOT explained by this run's coarse (nside=64, binary) angular mask -- it is a 3D (or angular-completeness-scale-finer-than-nside-64) feature that the lognormal recipe's single-bias, linear-theory model does not reproduce. This supports reading the gate failure as 'this simple mock recipe does not capture the data's clustering SHAPE' rather than 'the mask is broken' -- though a genuine sub-nside-64 angular completeness effect (SDSS fiber-plate boundaries, ~1-2 degree scale) remains possible and is NOT ruled out by this test, since it operates below this mask's own resolution.
angular_vs_3d_origin_of_the_xi_bump_at_r.tier: X, single random catalogue (not the full 4x/20-seed treatment), run for diagnosis only.

known_limitations_of_this_run: (1) The rank p-value (p=0.043 for H0, H1, H2) integrates STAT_R_RANGE=(2,40) Mpc/h, which INCLUDES r<~5 Mpc/h -- below this sample's mean inter-galaxy spacing (~5 Mpc/h at N=25000 in this volume) and so shot-noise/discreteness dominated. Individual mock Betti-curve arrays were not saved to disk in this run (only aggregate L2/envelope statistics), so the r<5 vs r>=5 contribution to p=0.043 cannot be decomposed after the fact; a re-run with the mock stacks saved (now straightforward to add) is needed to know how much of the headline p-value is a small-scale-discreteness effect versus a genuine large-scale topology difference. (2) loo_l2 min/median/max (the mock-to-mock scatter used for the rank test) were likewise not saved for the H0/H1/H2 rank-pvalue entries in THIS run's JSON; the source has been fixed (real_l2_over_median_loo_l2, loo_l2_min_median_max fields added to rank_pvalue_leave_one_out) for the next run, so a reader of THIS report cannot yet tell whether the real data's L2 is barely above the mock spread or many multiples of it.
